name: Drinking & cooking water
notes: Covers drinking plus rehydrating meals and hot drinks. Food-grade jerrycans or sealed bottles; leave ~10% headroom so a hard frost won't split them. Keep off the concrete floor.

name: Bottled water kept indoors
notes: Backup in case the garage stock freezes solid in a cold snap. Rotate into everyday use.

name: Collapsible water carriers
notes: For collecting and treating water if mains supply stops.

name: Water filter + purification tablets
notes: Tablets as backup to the filter. Don't let a filter with water in it freeze – store it dry.

name: Backpacking meals – lunch & dinner
notes: Counted on Food Store sheet: only 3 in-date protein mains (plus 12 Idahoan mash pots as sides). Need ~15 more. Each needs ~0.5 L boiling water.

name: Breakfasts – porridge pots / sachets, granola
notes: Porridge sachets are light, cheap and long-dated.

name: Tinned protein – tuna, chicken, ham, beans, chilli
notes: Edible cold if fuel runs short. Ring-pull tins where possible.

name: Tinned soup & vegetables
notes: Hot soup is a big morale boost in a winter power cut.

name: Snacks – cereal bars, nuts, trail mix, chocolate
notes: Chocolate can bloom in summer heat – rotate before July.

name: Peanut butter / spreads
notes: Check for allergies.

name: Hot drinks – tea, coffee, hot chocolate, sugar
Oral rehydration sachets
notes: Store indoors with medicines.

name: Seasoning – salt, pepper, stock cubes, sauce sachets
Comfort food / treats
notes: Worth it for morale, especially with children.

name: Dog food & treats (both dogs)
notes: Plus ~1 L extra water per dog per day. Sealed tub – dog food attracts rodents.

name: Gas canisters
notes: Use winter-mix (isobutane/propane) – plain butane struggles below ~0°C. Warm canisters indoors before use in cold weather.

name: Wood stoves
notes: Keep fuel off the floor and dry.

name: Dry fuel, kindling, firelighters
notes: Keep fuel off the floor and dry.

name: Lighters + storm-proof matches
notes: Matches in a waterproof tub.

name: Manual tin openers
notes: Easy to forget and essential if you rely on tins.

name: Portable solar panels
notes: Test quarterly.

name: Battery packs / power banks
notes: Keep at 50–80% and top up every 3 months. Lithium cells dislike being charged below 0°C – bring indoors to charge.

name: Paraffin lamps + paraffin
notes: Approved container, ventilated, away from gas. Only use indoors with ventilation and a CO alarm.

name: Head torches
notes: Hands-free is far more useful than a hand torch.

name: Spare batteries (AA / AAA)
notes: Lithium AAs cope best with cold storage.

name: Wind-up or battery DAB/FM radio
notes: Key for official updates if mobile and broadband are down.

name: Portable power station
notes: Pairs with the solar panels. Keep 50–80% charged and check quarterly.

name: Battery carbon monoxide alarm
notes: Essential if stoves or paraffin lamps are ever used indoors.

name: First aid kit
notes: Store indoors (heat and frost degrade contents).

name: Prescription medicines
notes: Indoors, not the garage.

name: Painkillers, antihistamines, diarrhoea relief
notes: Indoors.

name: Multi-tool, duct tape, cable ties, work gloves
Stopcock key / know shut-offs for gas, water, electricity
notes: Make sure every adult knows where they are.

name: Dust masks (FFP2/FFP3)
notes: For smoke, dust or contaminated air (FEMA).

name: Spare glasses / contact lenses
notes: Red Cross grab-bag item. An old prescription is fine.

name: Wet wipes
notes: Wash without water.

name: Heavy-duty bin bags
notes: Also make a makeshift toilet liner or rain cover.

name: Emergency toilet – lidded bucket, liners, cat litter
notes: For when toilets can't be flushed.

name: Sleeping bags & mats
notes: Store loose (not compressed) and dry.

name: Warm layers, hats, gloves, waterproofs
notes: Probably already in camping kit – just keep together.

name: Tarp / plastic sheeting + tape
notes: For broken windows or roof leaks.

name: Cash – coins and small notes
notes: Mix of coins and notes (Be Ready checklist). Card machines and ATMs fail in power cuts.

name: Copies of key documents (waterproof wallet)
notes: Indoors, in a grab bag – insurance, IDs, medical info.

name: Printed contact list + local paper map
notes: Include 105 (power cut line), utility suppliers, GP and neighbours' numbers – swap contacts with neighbours.

name: Grab bag per person
notes: For evacuation rather than staying put.

name: Written list of medication names & doses
notes: Be Ready checklist item – on paper, kept with document copies, in case phones and online records are unavailable.

name: Household emergency plan
notes: Use the Be Ready template: contacts, meeting point, who does what, where kit is kept. Talk it through with the family.

name: Priority Services Register – check eligibility
notes: Free. Register with your electricity and water suppliers if anyone in the household qualifies.

name: Lidded plastic crates (rodent-proof)
notes: Keep food out of cardboard – damp and mice.

name: Min/max thermometer
notes: Shows how hot and cold the garage really gets.

name: Moisture absorbers / silica gel
notes: Protects tins from rust and labels from damp.

name: Inventory with best-before dates
notes: Review every 6 months; eat oldest first and replace.

name: National Gas emergency
role: Gas leak or smell of gas

name: Water supplier
notes: Add the supplier and its emergency number.

name: GP surgery
notes: Add the surgery number.

name: School
notes: Add the school office number.

name: Neighbours
notes: Swap numbers with neighbours.

name: Home insurer
notes: Add the policy number and claims line.

name: Vet
notes: Add the practice and out-of-hours numbers.

name: Mountain House freeze-dried main meal pouches (mixed flavours)
notes: Maker's 30-year taste guarantee if kept below 24°C. Just add boiling water. Imported – Amazon UK or UK prepper shops.

name: Expedition Foods 'Survivor Foods' 25-year tins (UK alternative)
notes: UK-made (Hull). Bulk tin, so portion out once opened. Their standard pouches are only up to 5 years.

name: Rolled porridge oats
shelfLife: 1–2 yrs in packet; 20+ yrs resealed in Mylar
notes: Also thickens stews and makes flapjack-style snacks.

name: Non-fat milk powder
notes: Full-fat powder goes rancid far sooner.

name: Freeze-dried breakfast pouches (e.g. scrambled egg & bacon)
notes: A hot cooked breakfast boosts morale.

name: White rice (long grain / basmati)
fillsGap: Base for ~3 of the 6 cooked mains
shelfLife: 4–5 yrs in packet; 25+ yrs in Mylar with O₂ absorber
notes: White only – brown rice goes rancid within a year.

name: Dried pasta (egg-free)
fillsGap: Base for ~3 of the 6 cooked mains
notes: Egg pasta keeps less well.

name: Couscous
notes: Needs only boiling water – the most fuel-efficient carb.

name: Red lentils
notes: Cook in ~15 min with no soaking – good on limited gas.

name: Plain instant mashed potato flakes (bulk)
notes: Plain flakes outlast flavoured pots, which contain fats.

name: Freeze-dried meat – chicken and beef mince
notes: Add to rice, pasta or couscous with a sauce.

name: Tinned meat – corned beef, chicken, ham, chilli
fillsGap: No-cook meals (Be Ready asks for these)
notes: Ring-pull. Eat and replace once a year – the only items needing regular rotation.

name: Tinned fish – tuna, sardines, mackerel
notes: Rotate with the tinned meat.

name: Freeze-dried mixed vegetables (peas, carrots, sweetcorn)
notes: Rehydrate straight into the pan.

name: Tinned chopped tomatoes / passata
fillsGap: Sauce base for pasta, rice, lentils
notes: Rotate annually with the tins above.

name: Freeze-dried fruit (apple, strawberry)
notes: Good on porridge or straight from the pack.

name: Stock cubes (chicken, beef, veg)
fillsGap: Turns staples into soups and stews

name: Spice kit – curry powder, chilli flakes, mixed herbs, garlic granules, black pepper
notes: This is what makes the cooked meals different from each other.

name: Ghee or cooking oil
notes: Fats are the shortest-lived staple – rotate yearly.

name: Emergency ration bars (e.g. Datrex or SOS)
notes: Edible without water or fuel; withstand heat better than chocolate.

name: Freeze-dried desserts (e.g. custard, apple crumble)
notes: Treats matter in a long power cut.

name: Tea bags, instant coffee, hot chocolate
notes: Keep in an airtight tub.

name: Mylar bags + oxygen absorbers (or food-grade lidded buckets)
fillsGap: Lets rice, pasta, oats and lentils last 20+ years
notes: Repacking dry staples in Mylar with O₂ absorbers is what cuts down on rotation. Also stops mice.
